newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Call trade dominates BTPs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call trade dominates BTPs.

text.p: Call trading in options on June BTP futures dominated Italian debt options activity on Wednesday as the market shrugged off the country's political turmoil, traders on LIFFE said.

BTP futures broke out of a range, slicing through resistance around 127.40 to push through the 128.00 barrier. By 1415 GMT they were trading up 81 basis points at 127.85, off an earlier high of 128.08
"We were stuck in a range in the morning and BTPs are now following up the technical break," said a trader at a French brokerage.
A BTP futures trader said T-bond strength had fed through into the Bund market adding further support to the BTP rally.

Implied volatility spiked up to 8.30/8.44 percent for the June 127.50 straddle compared with 8.20 percent earlier in the day. The 128.00 strike was trading at a volatility of 8.0 percent, up 0.2 percent on the day.
The trader said it was the 130.00 strike June calls that had attracted most market interest.
More than 5,100, mostly traded in 1,000 lots, had been traded by 1415 GMT. Volatility at that strike flicked up to 7.6 percent from 7.5 percent earlier.
Traders said overall BTP volatilities were 0.5 percent higher than a week ago.
Although traders said they were keeping an eye on the Italian domestic scene, there were few signs that the market would turn negative on it.
Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi put his job on the line earlier on the issue of sending Italian-led security forces to Albania.
He said he would ask Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro to decide his fate if coalition partner the Communist Refoundation party deserted him in Wednesday's vote, expected around 1800 GMT.

"There's a lot of good feeling about BTPs, and Albania isn't going to derail that," said a trader at a U.S. bank. "The domestic issues such as pensions and the Maastricht criteria are of far more interest."
On the put side, the 125.00 strike took the lion's share of trade. Around 3,500 lots were traded with about 1,600 at the 127.50 strike.
